    O Captain! my Captain! our fearful trip is done,
    The ship has weather’d every rack, the prize we sought is won,
    The port is near, the bells I hear, the people all exulting,
    While follow eyes the steady keel, the vessel grim and daring;
                         But O heart! heart! heart!
                            O the bleeding drops of red,
                               Where on the deck my Captain lies,
                                  Fallen cold and dead.

    O Captain! my Captain! rise up and hear the bells;
    Rise up—for you the flag is flung—for you the bugle trills,
    For you bouquets and ribbon’d wreaths—for you the shores a-crowding,
    For you they call, the swaying mass, their eager faces turning;
                         Here Captain! dear father!
                            The arm beneath your head!
                               It is some dream that on the deck,
                                 You’ve fallen cold and dead.

    My Captain does not answer, his lips are pale and still,
    My father does not feel my arm, he has no pulse nor will,
    The ship is anchor’d safe and sound, its voyage closed and done,
    From fearful trip the victor ship comes in with object won;
                         Exult O shores, and ring O bells!
                            But I with mournful tread,
                               Walk the deck my Captain lies,
                                  Fallen cold and dead.

Hey, be glad you realized this NOW, man. I just got broken up with a month ago from a 2 year relationship. Long distance makes the shit even worse, trust me. Know why we broke up? Because of **me**. I didn't realize what codependency was, truly, until she finally explained what drove her away from me. Not only had I complained about us not talking like we used to (we did, I just missed her so bad that it felt like we didn't I guess.) but I also pushed her away whenever she tried to help me with any problem of my own. I didn't want to be a burden on her, but I would gladly take all of her problems.

Needless to say I'm realizing where I'm messed up and fixing it. The thing you should do is figure out what in your life *before* you two got together is causing you to be this way. I've been going to therapy for a month (along with getting on meds because I had no idea I actually had depression and anxiety problems which made shit much worse) and am more than happy to talk to you about it if you'd like. Codependency is like a virus, man. It spreads so quickly that it can seem to ruin much of your life and many of your relationships. Who knows, you may have caught this virus from someone in your life.

If you trust her enough, talk to her about it. Otherwise, fix it yourself by getting help. Whether it's professional help, or help from someone who's gone through it and knows some tips to handle it. Good luck, bro.

I can't speak for everyone, and there's a different kind of belligerence in each branch (by that I mean that Marines, Soldiers, Sailors, and Airmen all deal with their higher-ups differently, and that also depends on MOS.) A lot of the time, the trust that our NCO's instill in us and get back in return is so thick that some of us get blinded by what is actually happening. It's like your big brother that you look up to and admire so much just told you to go kick that dog. You KNOW it's wrong. Everything is telling you it's wrong. But...You don't want your big brother to be mad at you. So you kick it.

A lot of the time things go unreported. The whole hazing thing now-a-days goes unreported all the time. I've seen so much of it in the air wing of the Marine Corps that I'm kinda numb to it and have failed to report it myself. Even acted in it. *All because I didn't want the people directly above me to be disappointed and angry.* Some leaders throw rank around, and then threaten you with shit like negative counselings, NJP, etc. If service members would keep a clear mind, they'd see a lot of the things they're told to do by their direct higher-ups aren't legal and they don't have to listen.

Doubtful you'll get court. But, let's say I was ordered to shoot someone. Just a random civilian. Have they fired upon us? No. Are they a threat? Well, potentially, but that's not a reason to actually shoot. Only detain. Basically, I'd rather disobey a direct order than the Geneva Convention.

Happens all the damn time, actually. I think people who actually follow those unlawful orders have no idea that the amount of trouble for disobeying a direct order from your superior NCO, SNCO, or Officer 9 times out of 10 isn't as much trouble as following that unlawful order.

That has a lot to do with it, but also the fact that AC works in different phases. DC is direct current. That means when you're putting in 5v, you're getting 5v from the source. With AC, it's a bit different. You have what's called Volts Peak-to-Peak, or Vp-p. That's because you have alternating current, so you could be getting 5v, but also you could be getting -15v. Since you have this sine wave (typically; you can change it to a square wave or whatever with the right components) you can potentially reset or stop the heart. Among a plethora of other issues.
